answers.text: Family, a couple of close friends, cooking. I think I might want to cook for a living but I have only helped at a cafe twice. I want enough time for people even if sport gets more serious.
Quiet gets taken as not having an opinion. Usually I have one, I am working out how to say it. With my two best friends I am the one who talks most.
Getting something a little better and knowing people can rely on me. I made the same bread four weekends until it came out how I wanted. I do not care much about being the person everyone watches.
A small group is good. Big team days are fun and then I need an evening without plans. I like new people better if we are doing something together.
I listen first. If nobody has a plan I will suggest one, usually by asking if it works for everyone. In class I sometimes miss the chance because the conversation has moved on.
I write the options down and talk to one person. I chose fewer weekend shifts so I could keep swimming and see friends. It took a few days. I still wonder whether I should have saved more money.

I want to understand the first bit before trying. New recipes are fun because I can read the whole thing. I went kayaking without knowing much last summer because my friend was there and it was just for fun.
I like knowing the week. I keep a list on my phone. If a practice changes I move things around. A sudden change is annoying mainly because I may have promised someone else a time.
I usually finish if I said I would. I did a boring part of a class project because it was mine. Sometimes I spend too long making a small part perfect and start the next thing late.
An example I can work through. I asked a teacher to show one maths question, then checked mine against it. I use timers when baking. Asking in front of the class is harder.
Specific and preferably one to one. I appreciate an explanation. If someone only says good job I do not know what worked. I can take a direct correction once I have a moment to think.
I get even quieter and say I am fine too soon. Inside I might be replaying it. Last month a friend asked twice and I told him I was upset about a missed turn.
I put it off if it seems small. A friend kept changing our meeting time and I finally said it was messing up my plans. He said he had not realised. We agreed to decide the night before.
After a disappointing swim I look for the bit I can understand. That time I watched the turn with my coach the next day. On the night I just wanted dinner and no analysis.
I notice if someone has not had a turn to speak and ask them. I keep track of what we said we would do. I do not love assigning jobs, but I asked someone else to check our project references.
Checking things. I can check an email twice and still wait to send it. In cooking I am less careful with recipes I know. I change those just to see what happens.
People following through or telling me early if they cannot. I try to do that. I sometimes say yes because I do not want to cause trouble and then have to sort out too much.
I narrow in on one mistake. I can do the other parts but keep thinking about that bit. On a normal day I can leave it and move on. If someone wants an instant explanation I struggle to find words.
A packed weekend and lots of last minute messages. Cooking with music or walking with a friend helps. Exams are coming up so I need more quiet time than usual.
I do like competing. Being quiet does not mean I only want to participate. I want to improve my times, and I can be stubborn about a decision after I have thought it through.

questions.prompt: What matters most to you outside sport?
questions.followup: What would you like your life to make room for, now or later?

questions.prompt: What do people sometimes get wrong about you?
questions.followup: What would they understand better if they heard your side?

questions.prompt: What makes you want to put effort into something?
questions.followup: Tell us about something you chose to do, and something you found hard to care about.

questions.prompt: After spending time with other people, how do you usually feel?
questions.followup: Is it different with close friends and an unfamiliar group?

questions.prompt: In a group, how do you usually get involved?
questions.followup: When do you speak up, choose a direction, or leave room for someone else?

questions.prompt: When a choice is difficult, how do you decide?
questions.followup: Think of a recent choice. What mattered, and how long did you need?

questions.prompt: How do you approach something new or unfamiliar?
questions.followup: What makes you curious, and what makes you hold back?

questions.prompt: How much of a plan do you like before you start?
questions.followup: What happened the last time your plan changed?

questions.prompt: When something gets boring or difficult, what do you do?
questions.followup: Describe a time you kept going, changed your approach, or decided to stop.

questions.prompt: When you do not understand something, what do you try?
questions.followup: What happened the last time? Did another person or a tool help?

questions.prompt: What kind of feedback is easiest for you to use?
questions.followup: Describe feedback that helped, and anything that made it harder to take in.

questions.prompt: When you are upset, what might someone else notice?
questions.followup: What might they miss? Only tell us what you want to share.

questions.prompt: When you disagree with someone, what usually happens?
questions.followup: Can you remember an example, including what the other person actually said or did?

questions.prompt: After a disappointment, what helps you find your footing?
questions.followup: What happened on one occasion? It is okay if you are still figuring this out.

questions.prompt: What do you bring to a group that is useful?
questions.followup: Think of school, home, friends or sport. How do you share the work?

questions.prompt: When can one of your strengths get in your way?
questions.followup: How do you notice it, and is there a situation where it works differently?

questions.prompt: What makes you feel respected or fairly treated?
questions.followup: How do you try to offer that to someone else?

questions.prompt: What changes about you when the pressure rises?
questions.followup: Compare an ordinary situation with a difficult one. What was going on around you?

questions.prompt: What drains you, and what helps you feel like yourself again?
questions.followup: Is anything about your current week making a difference?

questions.prompt: What else should MORE understand about you?
questions.followup: Where have your answers missed the full picture? What are you still figuring out?
